reviewers.summary: The added checks close the direct local and variable reference case, but an interpolated local principal ID still lets an extra AcrPush grant to the app identity pass the test.

findingList.message: The local-reference gap remains for interpolated principal IDs. Cover evaluated references or reject interpolation forms so an extra ACR grant to the app identity fails the test.

evidence.codePathTraced: The new assertion detects direct local.* and var.* references in role assignments. The existing app-grant count only recognizes the literal azurerm_user_assigned_identity.app.principal_id address.
evidence.failureScenario: If an extra AcrPush assignment uses principal_id = "${local.app_principal_id}", with that local resolving to the app identity's principal ID and scope set directly to azurerm_container_registry.acr.id, the new regex does not match the quoted interpolation and the existing count omits the assignment. The test passes while the app identity can push images, contrary to AC RELEASE-ID-01 (OWASP A01:2025 Broken Access Control).

reviewers.summary: The round-4 fix catches direct local and variable references, but an indirect principal expression can still bypass the app identity grant checks.

findingList.message: AC RELEASE-ID-01 still permits an extra ACR grant when the app identity principal is referenced through a Terraform function around a local or variable. Detect evaluated assignments or reject indirect principal expressions.

evidence.codePathTraced: The app-grant count detects direct references to the app identity. This added check detects only principal_id expressions beginning directly with local. or var.; the scope check accepts a direct ACR scope.
evidence.failureScenario: If an extra AcrPush assignment uses principal_id = coalesce(local.app_principal_id, "...") where the local resolves to the app identity, and scope = azurerm_container_registry.acr.id, the new check does not match the wrapped local expression. The other checks miss it too, so the test passes with an extra ACR grant to the app identity.

reviewers.summary: The added guard catches dot-style local and variable references, but an indexed local reference can bypass the ACR assignment checks and leave an extra grant undetected.

findingList.message: The AC RELEASE-ID-01 check still misses an extra ACR grant when the principal uses Terraform local index syntax. Cover valid indexed local references so an additional grant fails the test.

evidence.codePathTraced: The new guard detects local or variable references only when written with dot syntax, and the assignment count also requires a direct app principal reference.
evidence.failureScenario: If an extra AcrPush assignment uses principal_id = local["app_principal_id"] with scope = azurerm_container_registry.acr.id, Terraform can grant the app identity push access while the local-reference guard and direct-reference count both miss it. The test can pass despite AC RELEASE-ID-01. This is an A01:2025 Broken Access Control regression.
